classification.difficultyReason: Follow the prompted chain from Pythagoras to a cosine-rule angle, then recognise that the block's area is the sum of a right triangle and a triangle requiring the sine area rule.

content.prompt: An irregular block of land, $ABCD$, has dimensions shown opposite. Calculate, correct to one decimal place:

spec.description: Unshaded quadrilateral ABCD with A lower left, B above and slightly right of A, C upper right and D directly below C. No diagonal is supplied. Ordinary blue source strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: AB=65 m, BC=90 m, CD=130 m, DA=80 m; angle ADC=90 degrees. Coordinates derive from the given lengths and preserve the convex source topology; no coordinate values print.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the four given side lengths, vertex names and right-angle marker are visible.

answer.worked:
In right-angled triangle $ADC$, by Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=80^2+130^2\\AC^2&=23300\\AC&=\sqrt{23300}\\AC&\approx152.6\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

Apply the cosine rule in triangle $ABC$, retaining $AC^2=23300$:
$$\begin{align*}\cos\angle ABC&=\frac{65^2+90^2-23300}{2(65)(90)}\\\cos\angle ABC&=-\frac{439}{468}\\\angle ABC&=\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{439}{468}\right)\\\angle ABC&\approx159.7^\circ.\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$6213.6\text{ m}^2$.

Split along $AC$ and add the areas of triangles $ADC$ and $ABC$.
answer.worked:
Split the block along $AC$. Let $\theta=\cos^{-1}(-\frac{439}{468})$, the unrounded angle from part b.
$$\begin{align*}A_{ADC}&=\frac12(80)(130)\\A_{ADC}&=5200\text{ m}^2\\A_{ABC}&=\frac12(65)(90)\sin\theta\\A_{ABCD}&=5200+\frac12(65)(90)\sin\left(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{439}{468}\right)\right)\\A_{ABCD}&\approx6213.6\text{ m}^2.\end{align*}$$
